bio.p_2: Hannah Berkeley Cohen is an Ohio native who has called the Caribbean home since 2012. After spending a semester abroad at the University of Havana, she moved to Cuba to document the country’s youth culture, the everyday life of the Cuban middle class, and the island’s dwindling Jewish community. By 2015, she had become the
bio.p_3: based in Havana, reporting on American foreign policy toward Cuba, the death of Fidel Castro, and the historic visits of President Obama and the Pope. In Havana, she met with dozens of groups organized by the JDC (American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee), synagogues across North America, and Jewish individuals returning for the first time to Cuba since their parents or grandparents left half a century earlier.
bio.p_4: Reporting for major media outlets gave Hannah rare access to Cuba’s layered society; in 2015, the ease in regulations for travel for Americans to Cuba allowed Hannah to share her insight of the island, with the goal of showcasing a nuanced Cuba: beyond rum, cigars, colorful buildings, and classic cars.

From meetings with ambassadors to conversations with black-market money exchangers, and culinary workshops with Michelin-starred chefs to cozy cooking lessons with grandmothers in modest home kitchens, Cuba Rising offered intimate cultural exchanges with people from all ranks of Cuban society. Each trip was highly customized, with group sizes capped at eight to ensure flexibility and depth of experience. Hannah is fluent in English and Spanish.
bio.p_8: Using her experience in Cuba, Hannah moved to Curaçao in 2024 to delve deeper into the Jewish history and heritage of the island, and create culturally-relevant programs for North American travelers.
bio.p_10: Born in the Netherlands and raised across Yugoslavia, Greece, and Cuba, Cornelis Greiwe developed an international outlook and love of travel early in life. He brings more than 20 years of entrepreneurial and leadership experience in the international tourism industry. Throughout his career, he has created distinctive travel products, worked with airlines to strengthen regional connectivity, and led hospitality projects across international markets. At the heart of his work is a passion for creating meaningful experiences that connect people, cultures, and networks.
bio.p_11: While managing his tour company in Havana, Cornelis founded and produced HAVANA PLAY, a groundbreaking series of electronic music events that provided emerging Cuban DJs and producers with a platform to connect with the international electronic music community. During its year-long run, HAVANA PLAY became the most widely-attended weekly music event in Cuba.
bio.p_12: After living and working in both Cuba and Suriname, Cornelis fell in love with Curaçao. He came to understand not only the vital role tourism plays in a small-island economy, but also the potential of cultural tourism to help shape a more sustainable future for the sector. Inspired by Curaçao’s extraordinary cultural diversity and layered heritage, he chose to make the island his home and the focus of his work. Today, he creates thoughtful, culture-forward programs that invite visitors to engage more deeply with the island, its history, and its people.
bio.p_13: Cornelis is fluent in English, Dutch, Spanish, and German.
